ctas.txt: For 13 days, Saint-Malo moves to the beat of the Route du Rhum: concerts, activities for all ages, sporting events and highlights.
Dive into the heart of one of France's biggest event villages: 70,000 m², the stands, the events and your favourite skippers.
Access, transport, parking, opening hours, services and handy tips to plan your day in Saint-Malo with ease.

questions.q: What is the Route du Rhum course?
p: A solo transatlantic race from **Saint-Malo to Pointe-à-Pitre**: about **3,542 nautical miles**, or 6,560 km. The fleet crosses the Channel, rounds Ushant, heads down into the Bay of Biscay, plays with the Azores high and then picks up the trade winds. A lap of Guadeloupe from the north is compulsory before the finish.

src.texte: What is the Route du Rhum?

questions.q: What kinds of boats take part?
p: Six classes start together: **Ultim**, **Ocean Fifty**, **IMOCA**, **Class40**, and two new classes in 2026, **Vintage Mono** and **Vintage Multi**, which replace the former Rhum categories and bring legendary boats back to sea.

questions.q: How long does the race last, and what is the record?
p: The record belongs to **Charles Caudrelier**, winner in 2022: **6 days 19 hours 47 minutes and 25 seconds** aboard the Ultim Maxi Edmond de Rothschild. The smallest boats take several weeks: the fleet arrives in Guadeloupe in stages.

src.texte: What is the Route du Rhum?

questions.q: Do professionals and amateurs really start together?
p: Yes. The race brings together professionals and amateurs, women and men, on the same start line, something rare in top-level sport. In 2022, **138 skippers** started and **103** made it to Pointe-à-Pitre.

src.texte: What is the Route du Rhum?

questions.q: Where and when do the boats arrive?
p: Finishes are celebrated at the **Mémorial ACTe**, in Pointe-à-Pitre, which has welcomed every skipper since 2018, from the first to the last. The first boats are expected **from 5 November 2026**.
Yes, three: at the **Mémorial ACTe**, at the **Bas-du-Fort marina** and in **Basse-Terre**, for three weeks of celebration.

questions.q: When does the race start, and at what time?
p: The race starts on **Sunday 1 November 2026 at 1:02 pm**, off Saint-Malo, with 115 skippers on the start line.

src.texte: What is the Route du Rhum?

questions.q: When is the village open, and at what times?
p: The village is open from **Tuesday 20 October** to **Sunday 1 November**: thirteen days of celebration over 70,000 m² around the harbour basins. Exhibitors open at 10 am (at noon on the first day). In the evening, **a small part of the village stays open late** for partying, until 1 am:
• **Tuesday 20 October**: exhibitors from noon to 8 pm, late night from 8 pm to 1 am
• **Wednesday 21 and Thursday 22**: exhibitors from 10 am to 8 pm, late night from 8 pm to 1 am
• **Friday 23 and Saturday 24**: exhibitors from 10 am to 10 pm, late night from 10 pm to 1 am
• **Sunday 25 to Thursday 29**: exhibitors from 10 am to 8 pm, late night from 8 pm to 1 am
• **Friday 30 and Saturday 31**: exhibitors from 10 am to 10 pm, late night from 10 pm to 1 am
• **Sunday 1 November**, race start day: from 10 am to 5 pm

questions.q: Is entry free? Do I need a ticket or a pass?
p: Yes, entry is **100% free, with no ticket**: no pass or booking needed, and the village is open to everyone.
There will be **systematic bag checks** at the entrance.

questions.q: Can I see the boats and go on the pontoons?
p: The boats of all six classes are moored in the basins, at the heart of the village, class by class. The interactive map shows where each of them is, pontoon by pontoon.

For safety reasons, **access to the pontoons is restricted to accredited people**. The public can still win a few accreditations by taking part in the many competitions run on the race's social media.

questions.q: How do I get to the village without a car?
p: By bus, Saint-Malo's network costs **€1.40** online or at a sales point, **€2** on board. By bike, secure bike parks are waiting at **every entrance** to the village, and shared e-bikes are available all over town.
The page has a tool that finds your best route depending on the region you are coming from.

questions.q: Are dogs allowed at the village?
p: We love our four-legged friends 🐾, but for everyone's safety and comfort, **dogs are not allowed at the village**. Only assistance dogs accompanying a person with a disability are permitted.
